text:
The Red Wings' season is defined by who doesn't want to be there. Dylan Larkin, the former captain, asked for a trade, told the team he would not play for Detroit again, and was suspended without pay on Oct. 29. The banner with his likeness outside the arena has been replaced with one of Emmitt Finnie. Simon Edvinsson, unsigned after a contract stalemate, has also made clear he would prefer to go, and The Hockey Writers now adds a third name to the exit list.

On the ice, the team is 8-12-3 and 2-8-0 in its last 10. Our numbers say it is better than that: Detroit has 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) but has scored about 12 fewer goals than those chances predict, and our standings model has it more than four points short of what its play deserves. Viktor Arvidsson (1 point in 10, 7.8 expected) and Alex DeBrincat (2 in 10, 8.5 expected) are the coldest of the cold.

Daniil Tarasov has done his part, with a .927 and 3.8 goals saved above expected over his last five starts, and has a 1-4-0 record to show for it. The DeBrincat, Finnie and Michael Brandsegg-Nygard trio has taken 63% of the expected goals and outscored teams 8-1.

Our playoff odds have Detroit at 10%. What we'd watch: whether the shooters' luck turns before the front office makes the Larkin move.
